h: Pemberley's interiors and a gallery to make you gasp
p: Period drama fans, listen up. Sudbury Hall's interiors were used as Pemberley in the BBC's 1995 adaptation of Pride and Prejudice, the one with Colin Firth and that lake scene. The lake itself was filmed elsewhere, but plenty of the grand rooms you see on screen are right here, so you can play spot-the-scene as you go round.

The house was built from the 1660s by George Vernon, and he went all out. The Long Gallery is a real showstopper, with elaborate plasterwork running the length of the room, and the main staircase is one of those pieces of craftsmanship that makes you stop and stare. Even if you're only half interested in architecture, it's hard not to be impressed.
Sudbury village itself is a neat little estate village and worth a short wander while you're there.

Allow at least half a day if you want to do the house, the Museum of Childhood and the grounds properly. With kids, splitting it up with a picnic in the middle stops anyone running out of steam. Bring a coat for the gardens and good shoes for the walk between buildings.

If you're making a weekend of it, Ashbourne puts you right on the doorstep of Dovedale, with its famous stepping stones over the River Dove. Tutbury Castle is just over the border in Staffordshire, and Alton Towers is close enough to tempt thrill-seekers into a second day.
